subject: Private fleet: slab commitment vs network slit — provisioning alignment
messages:
From: Samir Gupta <samir.gupta@brightlane.ai>
To: irene_choi@redwood.com, karthik_iyer@redwood.com
Cc: ops@brightlane.ai
Date: Tue, 14 Apr 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Quick: private cluster headroom + network slit for DL-4782

Irene / Karthik — thanks again for the afternoon call yesterday. Two quick asks so we can finalize our procurement window with infra: 

1) We need a concise provisioning target (GPU count + slab commit) that meets the peak throughput SLA we're negotiating: 8k concurrent requests sustained with P95 < 180ms for 2k-token median requests.
2) BrightLane networking says they'll enforce a "slit" on cross-rack egress (per-rack egress cap ~6 Gbps). Can you confirm whether our admission and batching plan tolerates that for the proposed slab?

Attaching our current traffic profile (median/95th percentile token sizes + qps distribution). We prefer a numeric answer (e.g., N x A100 80GB, warm pool size M, admission threshold T) so procurement can convert to an order.

Can you get back today? We're in a contract window with our procurement team.

— Samir
Lead, Platform Ops — BrightLane

Attachments: brightlane_traffic_profile.csv (referenced)

From: irene_choi@redwood.com
To: Samir Gupta <samir.gupta@brightlane.ai>
Cc: karthik_iyer@redwood.com, laura_bennett@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 14 Apr 2026 11:07:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Quick: private cluster headroom + network slit for DL-4782

Samir — thanks, reviewed the profile. High level answer up front: we can meet the SLA with a conservative slab of 12 x A100-80GB (or equivalent v4 units), with a warm-pool of 2 racks (recommended min 2 racks for rack-failure tolerance). Operational knobs:

- Target sustained throughput: ~11k tokens/sec per GPU at median request (with our optimized runtime and continuous batching).
- Admission threshold: set at 85% of slab nominal qps to preserve 30% burst headroom; for the 12-GPU slab that maps to a soft cap of ~85 concurrent inference pipelines per GPU (approx).
- KV-cache warmup: expect first-request penalty ~180–260ms if cache cold; warm-pool + prefix caching reduces tail.
- Batching behavior: use adaptive micro-batching with max latency budget 100ms to keep p95 under 180ms for 2k tokens when admission holds.

Network slit / egress piece: with per-rack egress capped to ~6 Gbps we need to distribute live serving across at least two racks to avoid hitting per-rack egress limits during heavy embedding/response scenarios. Practical mapping:

- Deploy slab across 3 racks (4 GPUs/rack). Each rack should have 6–8 Gbps reserved for inference egress (we recommend 8 Gbps to leave margin).
- If customers do heavy streaming (many tokens per response), add an Egress QOS policy to prioritize small control messages; stream payloads should be chunked to avoid long dominant flows.

I've attached: 1) quick calc (privfleet_provisioning_calc_v1.xlsx) mapping slab sizes to expected tokens/sec and egress bandwidth, 2) a simple rack-slit topology (vpc_network_slit_diagram.pdf).

Action items for procurement: order commit for 12 A100 equiv for initial slab; include 2 additional spare GPUs for warm-pool (recommend 14 physical GPUs). For the contract duration, we can propose staged capacity increases based on actual run-rate (30% buffer).

I'll leave Karthik and Laura to sanity-check the per-GPU throughput numbers and the network assumptions.

— Irene Choi
Principal Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference
Phone: +1-415-555-0126

Attachments: privfleet_provisioning_calc_v1.xlsx, vpc_network_slit_diagram.pdf

From: karthik_iyer@redwood.com
To: Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.com>, Samir Gupta <samir.gupta@brightlane.ai>
Cc: laura_bennett@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 14 Apr 2026 13:02:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Quick: private cluster headroom + network slit for DL-4782

Irene — numbers look reasonable. A few notes from infra/ops perspective: 

- Per-GPU throughput: our internal microbenchmarks (A100-80GB, qkv fused kernels) show ~10.5–11.5k tokens/sec for short/median sequences; heavy 2k token tails bring effective per-GPU throughput down ~18–22% depending on batching efficiency. I've baked a conservative 20% degradation into the spreadsheet.
- Egress calc: 12 GPUs distributed across 3 racks yields a theoretical maximum egress demand of ~18 Gbps under worst-case streaming (assuming 1 token ~1.5 bytes post-encoding). With per-rack slit at 6 Gbps, the steady-state should be fine as long as streaming overlap isn't perfectly correlated across racks. We should add a per-tenant shaping rule to smooth correlated peaks.
- Admission control: set soft limit at 0.6*max_sustained_qps during onboarding; once telemetry confirms steady latency & tail behavior, raise to 0.85. That avoids surprise saturation on day-1.
- Thermal/ops: recommend 1 reserve rack in the same POD to allow rolling upgrades and quick failover during hardware grief.

Samir — I'd like to schedule a 30-min follow-up to lock down the exact order quantities (GPUs vs. spare warm pool) and the QOS knobs BrightLane will expose. Tomorrow at 10am PT works for us.

— Karthik
Head of Solutions Engineering, Redwood Inference

From: laura_bennett@redwood.com
To: karthik_iyer@redwood.com, Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.com>, Samir Gupta <samir.gupta@brightlane.ai>
Date: Tue, 14 Apr 2026 15:04:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Quick: private cluster headroom + network slit for DL-4782

Thanks everyone — echoing Karthik's staged approach. A crisp note for procurement and BrightLane ops: 

- Recommended initial contract: commit to 12 active GPUs + 2 warm spares, 12-month term, with a 8-week right to scale up at pre-agreed pricing if run-rate crosses 65% sustained for two consecutive weeks.
- SLO guardrails: p95 < 180ms for 2k median request, with emergency throttles and fallback model (smaller quantized variant) if admission fails.
- Security/compliance: ensure VPC egress ACLs allow our monitoring collector IP range; we'll provide a minimal SOC2 evidence bundle but please surface any additional registry requirements.

Samir — can you confirm procurement can accept the 8-week scale clause? If yes, we'll draft an MOU and attach the capacity & QOS appendix.

— Laura Bennett
Director, Enterprise Partnerships, Redwood Inference
